text: Yes, the 2022 loss was detected with Sentinel-2 imagery. The Hansen Global Forest Change dataset (GFC-2025-v1.13), which uses Sentinel-2 data, confirmed a tree-cover loss event in 2022. The loss area was 0.6 hectares, meeting the minimum event size threshold of 0.5 hectares. The JRC dataset corroborated the forest presence in 2020, while the MGAP map confirmed the area was native forest. Although 0.2 hectares of loss occurred in patches smaller than 0.5 hectares (not counted as an event), the remaining 0.4 hectares qualified as a detectable loss in 2022.
